title: Uncovering Non-Gaussianity through Multi-Copy Symmetries
abstract: Gaussian states are fundamental in continuous-variable quantum information, yet characterizing non-Gaussianity remains challenging due to the non-convexity of the Gaussian set. Existing witnesses typically rely on Wigner negativity or other information-theoretic quantities. In this work, we develop a group-theoretic, multi-copy approach to detect non-Gaussianity in bosonic systems. We study passive linear optical transformations that mix copies of a quantum state and analyze their commutation with identical Gaussian unitaries applied to each copy. Orthogonal copy-mixing transformations commute with the symplectic part of the Gaussian action, while the displacement part restricts the symmetry to the stabilizer of the collective mode. This structure yields a family of witnesses satisfied by all single-mode Gaussian states. Fixing the thermal reference parameter via the purity, violation of these identities certifies non-Gaussianity. We illustrate the method with several single-mode examples and present an experimental protocol based on passive interferometry and photon-number-resolved detection, showing that the relevant multi-copy expectation values can be estimated from bounded phase observables. Finally, we extend the construction to multi-mode systems and discuss how the same symmetry framework may lead to quantitative measures of non-Gaussianity.
summary: This paper introduces a novel group-theoretic approach using multi-copy symmetries to diagnose non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states. By analyzing how copy-mixing transformations interact with Gaussian unitaries, the authors derive necessary symmetry identities that all Gaussian states must obey. Violation of these identities provides a concrete and experimentally testable witness for non-Gaussian character.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a robust method to characterize non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum states, as traditional witnesses struggle due to the non-convex nature of Gaussian sets.
main_result: The authors developed a group-theoretic, multi-copy symmetry framework where violating specific identities derived from copy-mixing transformations certifies that a state is non-Gaussian.
method: The method analyzes how passive linear optical transformations mixing multiple copies of a quantum state commute with Gaussian unitaries applied to each copy, leading to symmetry constraints violated by non-Gaussian states.
model_or_system: The work focuses on bosonic systems (single-mode and multi-mode) described by continuous variables, utilizing concepts from Lie groups like the Heisenberg group and symplectic transformations.

important_parameters: The number of copies ($k$), the thermal reference parameter (fixed via purity), and parameters defining the covariance matrix ($\sigma$) are crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the relevant symmetry structure can be captured by analyzing commutators involving copy-mixing transformations and Gaussian unitaries, which is extended to multi-mode systems.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the difficulty of non-Gaussianity witnesses to developing a group-theoretic framework based on copy-mixing symmetries. It derives specific commutation relations for Gaussian states and then proposes using violations of these identities as quantitative detectors, culminating in an experimental protocol.
why_interesting: This provides a powerful, mathematically rigorous tool rooted in symmetry theory (group theory) to detect non-Gaussianity in continuous variable systems, which is highly relevant for quantum optics and quantum information processing.
